title: render-backends: four-criteria ship bar + pdf determinism pinning
description:
Grilling decision D4 (wai: .wai/projects/sunshine/designs/2026-11-16-title-sunshine-alignment-decisions-audit-firs.md): 'shipped' for a backend = ALL FOUR, enforced by just ci — (1) totality: renders every manifest the anchor.manifest strict parser accepts; unsupported input is a named refusal at render time, never silent subset behavior; (2) round-trip green: audit(render(m)) == m over the generated suite; (3) suite envelope present per render.contract; (4) deterministic bytes: byte-reproducible output for the same inputs.

Why totality: without it the governing property has a hidden per-backend precondition nothing in the manifest records; the stamp would need backend identity, complicating ac_manifest_identity. p_roundtrip's 'no backend reaches shipped state' wording stays consistent — this constraint defines what shipped means.

Landmine to pin NOW (not at sun-4y6 pickup): real PDFs embed creation timestamps and document IDs that break determinism. Pdf may ship only if all embedded time/IDs are derived from the manifest digest. If that is unacceptable, pdf cannot ship at all — decided now, not at P3.

Spec edit: specs/render-backends.md
- Add invariant rb_ship_bar: a backend counts as shipped only when totality, round-trip, envelope, and byte-determinism all hold under just ci; absence of any one means unshipped. traces_to [[render.backends]].
- Add invariant rb_deterministic_pdf (or a per-profile constraint under the pdf profile row): every timestamp, document ID, and nondeterministic embedded value in pdf output is derived from the manifest digest; no wall-clock or random source may reach artifact bytes.
- Add deriving property rows per linter.coverage.

TDD: red = property rows first -> spk lint no_orphan_property fails; green = invariants land, just gates passes; refactor = re-read p_roundtrip and render-contract stamping rows for wording drift.
notes:
METER: just test && just gates; ah check --run-tests reports 0 failing.
GATES: new scenario ids from the added property rows go into tools/gates/ah-undeclared.txt (comment = this ticket) in the same change.
LEDGER: changed specs/render-backends.md (rb_ship_bar with pinned strict-parser domain + named machine-readable refusal + rc_envelope criterion; rb_deterministic_pdf digest pinning; p_ship_bar, p_deterministic_pdf) + mirrors + ratchet lines. verified: spk lint specs ok; just gates 6 passed / 54; RO5U 2 High/1 Medium/1 Low all fixed. Backend implementations land under sun-jh6/sun-14e/sun-4y6; pdf unshippability is now explicit.

title: audit-contract: unparseable-artifact refusal class (total auditor)
description:
Grilling decision D3 (wai: .wai/projects/sunshine/designs/2026-11-16-title-sunshine-alignment-decisions-audit-firs.md): a file with no render stamp / wrong shape / truncated is a distinct 'unparseable' refusal class INSIDE the contract — not a CLI usage error. Rationale: ac_deterministic makes audit a pure function of (artifact, manifest, profile); totality over file contents keeps that honest and the state machine closed. Usage errors are reserved for bad CLI args.

Spec edit: specs/audit-contract.md
- Define 'loaded' as: render stamp present + skeleton parse succeeded.
- Add invariant ac_unparseable: an artifact lacking a stamp or failing skeleton parse refuses with a distinct machine-readable class (unparseable) naming the remediation; never a panic, never a usage error, never silent.
- Add transition refuse_unparseable: loaded -> refused, guarded by [[audit.contract.ac_unparseable]].
- Add property p_unparseable (unit): generator = garbage/truncated/no-stamp/stamp-but-garbage files; predicate = every input yields refusal with class unparseable, byte-identical reports on repeat (ac_deterministic), exit nonzero mirrored in envelope.

Implementation of the parser-side behavior lands with the md audit parser (sun-14e); this ticket is the spec that gates it.

TDD: red = transition + property rows first -> spk lint fails (guard cites unresolved constraint / orphan property); green = constraint + state definition land, just gates passes; refactor = cross-check ac_manifest_identity ordering prose still consistent (digest check stays before parsing).
notes:

LEDGER: changed specs/audit-contract.md (ac_unparseable invariant; refuse_unparseable loaded->refused; p_unparseable; loaded defined as the pre-decision state in prose; canonicalization stripping scoped to formatting while comment payloads carrying claim bindings stay content; unparseable-before-profile precedence) + mirrors. verified: spk lint specs ok; just gates 6 passed / 54 declared-undeclared; cargo test 6 passed; RO5U 2 High/1 Medium/2 Low all fixed. parser behavior itself lands with sun-14e.

title: DECIDE: multi-episode claim export policy — primary locator vs per-episode span lists
description:
Rule-of-5 review finding EDGE-002 (TypeSafe-verified 0.89).

am_claim_fields admits lineage of >=1 episode ids but carries exactly one evidence_span and one locator. Export policy for claims grounded in several episodes is undefined and schema-shaping for sun-mqs.

Options:
(a) RECOMMENDED for v1 — one record per claim with a designated primary locator/span; lineage stays provenance (one claim, many supports).
(b) per-episode span lists (episode_id, span, locator tuples) — richer, layerable later as an optional field.

Land before sun-mqs schema freeze. This issue blocks sun-mqs.

title: DECIDE: episode-text home — descriptor-owned (recommended) vs self-contained manifest
description:
Rule-of-5 review finding CORR-002 (TypeSafe-verified 0.84).

am_strict_parse demands parse-time refusal of 'references to absent episodes', but manifest claim records carry only episode ids — episode text lives in the descriptor (ai_verbatim_text). So the check as placed is impossible without a schema change or a check relocation.

Options:
(a) RECOMMENDED — descriptor owns episode text; move the absent-episode refusal to the join stage (extend ai_descriptor_required or add a join-time invariant in anchored-ir). am_strict_parse keeps unknown-fields/duplicate-keys. Matches the sunset/bajan division; keeps manifests small.
(b) manifest carries an episodes registry (self-contained; strengthens 'rendering needs no store access'; larger manifests; audit could run manifest-only).

Land the decision as a corpus amendment (+ mirrors redeploy) BEFORE sun-mqs schema freeze. This issue blocks sun-mqs.
notes:
LANE: design (human judgment call — never AFK-schedulable).
CLOSE WHEN: decision landed as a corpus amendment (mirrors recompiled + redeployed, spk lint green) or explicitly rejected with rationale recorded here.
Meter: just gates green on the amended corpus.

title: DECIDE: --out overwrite policy — refuse without --force vs overwrite-always (EDGE-005)
description:
Spun out of sun-mkj bullet EDGE-005 (rule-of-5 review 2026-11-16).

DECISION: rendering onto an existing --out path.
- (a) refuse without an explicit --force (protects a human-edited artifact — which ac_human_edits treats as the correction signal).
- (b) overwrite always (keeps render a pure function with no interactive state; the correction signal must be copied first).

Record the rejected alternative in the design note; the choice also fixes whether rc_atomic_write needs a pre-existence check and whether a refusal class lands in the render envelope.

Land as a corpus amendment with deriving property rows, mirrors redeployed, just gates green, plus the ah baseline line naming this ticket.

title: DECIDE: pdf claims annex carriage for unanchored claims (EDGE-004)
description:
Spun out of sun-mkj bullet EDGE-004 (rule-of-5 review 2026-11-16).

DECISION: bk_pdf_annotations never says how unanchored claims (ai_unanchored) travel in a pdf.
- (a) annex page: unanchored claims get an appended page in the pdf, visible to a human reader.
- (b) manifest-only carriage: the claims ride the embedded manifest attachment; no visible annex page.

Tension to state in the record: D1 (machine auditability beats presentation unconditionally) permits either, but (a) makes the round-trip depend on annex layout while (b) leaves the artifact visually silent about unanchored claims. Whichever wins, the audit parser must name it, so the choice is corpus-level, not pdf-code-level.

Land as a corpus amendment with deriving property rows, mirrors redeployed, just gates green, plus the ah baseline line naming this ticket.

title: DECIDE: zero-claim manifest render — stamped no-op vs refusal (EDGE-003)
description:
Spun out of sun-mkj bullet EDGE-003 (rule-of-5 review 2026-11-16).

DECISION: what does render do for a valid, strictly-parsing manifest that carries zero claims?
- (a) valid stamped no-op: emit an artifact with the render stamp and an empty claims section (bajan ic_empty_stream precedent — empty is a state, not an error).
- (b) refusal: zero claims is a caller error, refused with a named class and remediation.

Why it cannot be decided in the implementation: it fixes whether rc_input_present/ac_deterministic stay total over the strict-parser domain (an empty manifest parses strictly) and whether the auditor's suite envelope has a zero-claim case at all.

Land the choice as a corpus amendment (specs/render-contract.md or specs/anchor-manifest.md) with deriving property rows, spk compile + tools/deploy_specs.py, just gates green, plus the ah baseline line naming this ticket.
